column1: # GE-T10's misread set: the questions every earlier set still reads as the wrong intent, which
# costs more than one left unread — an unread question says so, a misread one answers another.
# WHY. Swept from every set's report after rule 29 (1.12.0): "What is the origin of scurvy?" and
# "Was ist der Ursprung des Skorbuts?" read as definitions, by `what is` / `was ist`; "Erkläre
# mir den Begriff Cholera" as an explanation, by `erkläre`; "Was bewies Linds Versuch?" as an
# English verification, by the last-resort `was `, which rule 28 lets through because `was` is
# a word of both languages and the guess makes none.
# THE RULES, DECLARED before a word of this set was written; scored first without them
# (`baseline.txt`), and not changed after a run:
#  30. a trace asked by a thing's origin:
#        en  what is the origin of / what was the origin of / what are the origins of
#        de  was ist der ursprung / was war der ursprung
#        es  cuál es el origen / cuál fue el origen / cuáles son los orígenes
#        fr  quelle est l'origine / quelle était l'origine / quelles sont les origines
#        ru  каково происхождение / каким было происхождение
#  31. a definition asked as explaining a term:
#        en  explain the term / explain the word
#        de  erkläre mir den begriff / erkläre den begriff / erkläre das wort
#        es  explica el término / explícame el término / explica la palabra
#        fr  explique le terme / explique-moi le terme / explique le mot
#        ru  объясни термин / объясни понятие / объясни слово
#  32. a last-resort opener that is also one of `guess_lang`'s words for another language (`was`
#      is German too, `es` German too) reads a question only when the guess names its own
#      language; with no guess it does not read. Every other last-resort opener reads as rule 28
# THE SET. Columns as `../collide/`: qid, want, lang, question; `want` an intent, or `none` for
# a question no rule should read as a verification. Some rows reach for a form no rule writes
# (`woher stammt`, `откуда пришла`), as a person would. Two guards per rule: an explanation
# asked with `explain`, a definition asked with `what is`, and two English questions opening
# with `was` that rule 32 may cost — its price, scored rather than assumed.
# WHO WROTE THIS. The hand that declared the rules, after declaring them. Single hand.
